choices.text: Percutaneous coronary intervention in the cath lab

choices.label: D
choices.text: Permanent pacemaker placement in the cath lab

choices.label: E
choices.text: Surgical valve replacement in the operating room

explanation.summary: Percutaneous coronary intervention in the cath lab is one option for relieving ischemic chest pain when nitrates lose efficacy.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick's case conclusion notes that other therapies that could help relieve JD's chest pain include percutaneous coronary intervention in the cath lab, or potentially other medication therapy such as beta-blockers or calcium channel blockers.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cardioversion treats arrhythmias and is not mentioned as a therapy for angina.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pericardiocentesis treats pericardial effusion, not myocardial ischemia from coronary disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A pacemaker treats conduction problems, not ischemic chest pain.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Valve replacement addresses valvular disease, not coronary ischemia.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man on continuous nitrate therapy has developed tolerance. His physician considers simply increasing the nitrate dose. Which of the following best describes the expected consequence of this approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It can worsen side effects without necessarily preventing tolerance

choices.label: B
choices.text: It converts the short-acting drug into a long-acting formulation

choices.label: C
choices.text: It eliminates the need for a daily 10-12 hour nitrate-free interval

choices.label: D
choices.text: It reduces the risk of vasodilation-related headache and hypotension

choices.label: E
choices.text: It reliably reverses tolerance without any added adverse-effect risk

explanation.summary: Increasing the nitrate dose can lead to more severe side effects and does not necessarily prevent tolerance.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick's review explanation states that increasing the dosage can lead to more severe side effects and does not necessarily prevent tolerance. The magnitude of tolerance is a function of dosage and frequency of use, so higher continuous doses do not solve the problem; a 10-12 hour nitrate-free interval does.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Dose size does not change the formulation or its onset characteristics.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The nitrate-free interval remains the strategy that decreases tolerance; a higher dose does not replace it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Higher doses increase, not decrease, vasodilation-related effects such as headache and hypotension.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Increasing the dose does not reliably reverse tolerance and adds adverse-effect risk.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man with hyperlipidemia has developed chest pain with exertion over the past several months. Which of the following changes in his coronary vessels most directly explains the impaired oxygen delivery to his myocardium?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Excess nitric oxide production dilating the coronary arteries

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased cGMP in vascular smooth muscle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased venous return raising coronary perfusion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inflammation of the pericardium compressing the coronary arteries

choices.label: E
choices.text: Plaque buildup reducing the effective diameter of the coronary arteries

explanation.summary: Atherosclerotic plaque reduces the effective diameter of blood vessels, reducing blood flow and oxygen delivery to the myocardium.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick explains that atherosclerosis (plaque buildup) reduces the effective diameter of blood vessels, effectively reducing blood flow to the myocardium so that oxygen delivery to the heart becomes impaired. As plaques become unstable, grow, or other stressors are introduced, this can lead to ischemia and chest pain.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nitric oxide dilates vessels and improves supply; it does not cause the ischemia of angina.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Increased cGMP relaxes vascular smooth muscle and improves flow, the opposite of the ischemic process.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Increased venous return would not impair oxygen delivery; the problem is narrowed coronary vessels.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pericardial inflammation is not the mechanism of angina described in the brick.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with severely elevated blood pressure requires a nitrate that can acutely lower his blood pressure with a short onset of action. Which of the following formulations is most appropriate?

explanation.summary: IV nitroglycerin (like sodium nitroprusside) is used to acutely lower blood pressure.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick notes that in some instances nitrates such as IV nitroglycerin or sodium nitroprusside are used to acutely lower blood pressure. IV nitroglycerin is a short-acting agent with short onset, and its significant vasodilation can lower blood pressure quickly, which is why blood pressure must be monitored.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Isosorbide dinitrate has a delayed onset and is used for chronic angina.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Isosorbide mononitrate is slowly absorbed with delayed onset and is used for chronic angina.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The transdermal patch has a delayed onset due to transdermal absorption.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The sublingual tablet is used for acute angina; the brick identifies the IV agents as those used to acutely lower blood pressure.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man presents with new-onset chest pain at rest. His physician explains that unstable angina and myocardial infarction are grouped together under a single category of ischemic heart disease. Which of the following is that category?

explanation.summary: Acute coronary syndrome comprises myocardial infarction and unstable angina.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick's figure shows ischemic heart disease branching into acute coronary syndrome, which includes myocardial infarction and unstable angina, and separately into stable angina.

whyWrongByChoice.B: "Chronic" is the brick's label for stable angina, not for the grouping of unstable angina and MI.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Congestive heart failure is not part of the ischemic heart disease classification shown.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Stable angina is a separate branch of ischemic heart disease, outside acute coronary syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vasospastic angina is one of the three types of angina, not the category that contains myocardial infarction.

questions.stem: A medical student asks why it matters whether a patient's angina is classified as "acute" (unstable) or "chronic" (stable) before prescribing a nitrate. Which of the following best explains the clinical importance of this distinction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It determines whether a nitrate is indicated at all

choices.label: B
choices.text: It determines whether coronary or venous dilation occurs

choices.label: C
choices.text: It determines whether the drug is converted to nitric oxide

choices.label: D
choices.text: It determines whether the patient will develop headache

choices.label: E
choices.text: It determines which route of administration is chosen

explanation.summary: Whether angina is acute or chronic determines which nitrate route of administration is chosen.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that the acute-versus-chronic distinction is important for medication choice because it impacts which route of administration is chosen. Short-onset formulations such as sublingual tablets are used for acute angina, whereas slowly absorbed oral agents such as isosorbide mononitrate are used for chronic angina.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nitrates are indicated for both acute and chronic angina.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nitrates produce venous and some coronary dilation in all patients; the classification does not change this.
whyWrongByChoice.C: All nitrates are converted to nitric oxide regardless of the type of angina.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Headache relates to the rapidity of vasodilation of the formulation, not to the angina classification per se.

questions.stem: A resident is deciding how long a patient can remain on uninterrupted nitrate therapy before tolerance is likely to become a concern. According to the case discussion, after approximately how many hours of continuous nitrate use can patients develop nitrate tolerance?

explanation.summary: After 12-14 hours of continuous nitrate use, patients can develop nitrate tolerance.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick's case conclusion reminds the reader that after 12-14 hours of continuous nitrate use patients can develop nitrate tolerance. This is why the patch is worn for 12-14 hours and then removed for a 10-12 hour nitrate-free interval.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tolerance does not develop within the first 1-2 hours of a dose.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Tolerance develops within hours, not weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A 4-6 hour window is shorter than the 12-14 hour threshold the brick gives.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tolerance develops well before 48-72 hours of continuous exposure.

questions.stem: A researcher studies a patient with nitrate tolerance and finds that the vascular smooth muscle retains a normal capacity to convert nitroglycerin to nitric oxide. Which of the following best accounts for the diminished nitrate response in this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Activation of mechanisms outside the vessel wall

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased cGMP accumulation in smooth muscle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased guanylyl cyclase activity in smooth muscle

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reduced first-pass metabolism of the nitrate

choices.label: E
choices.text: True vascular tolerance of the smooth muscle

explanation.summary: Nitrate tolerance may arise either from true vascular tolerance or from activation of mechanisms extraneous to the vessel wall.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick describes two sources of nitrate tolerance: a reduced capacity of the vascular smooth muscle to convert nitroglycerin to NO (true vascular tolerance), or the activation of mechanisms extraneous to the vessel wall. When conversion to NO is intact, the second, extravascular mechanism is the explanation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Increased cGMP would strengthen vasodilation, the opposite of tolerance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Increased guanylyl cyclase activity would enhance, not diminish, the response.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reduced first-pass metabolism would raise drug exposure and increase, not decrease, effect.
whyWrongByChoice.E: True vascular tolerance specifically means reduced conversion of nitroglycerin to NO, which is preserved here.

questions.stem: Two patients receive nitroglycerin. One takes an occasional low-dose sublingual tablet; the other receives frequent high doses around the clock. The second patient develops far greater attenuation of drug effect. Which of the following pairs of factors determines the magnitude of nitrate tolerance?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Renal clearance and plasma protein binding

choices.label: D
choices.text: Route of administration and headache severity

choices.label: E
choices.text: Type of angina and coronary anatomy

explanation.summary: The magnitude of nitrate tolerance is a function of dosage and frequency of use.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that the magnitude of tolerance is a function of dosage and frequency of use. Frequently repeated or continuous exposure to high doses produces marked attenuation of nitrate effects, whereas intermittent low-dose use with nitrate-free intervals does not.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Age and body weight are not identified by the brick as determinants of tolerance magnitude.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Renal clearance and protein binding are not the factors the brick links to tolerance.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Headache severity is an adverse effect and does not determine tolerance; route matters only insofar as it affects continuous exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The type of angina influences route selection, not the magnitude of tolerance.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with erectile dysfunction and no correctable underlying cause is started on sildenafil. Which of the following best describes the mechanism by which this drug improves erectile function?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It activates guanylyl cyclase to increase production of cGMP

choices.label: B
choices.text: It blocks phosphodiesterase type 5 and reduces the breakdown of cGMP

choices.label: C
choices.text: It directly causes vasoconstriction within the corpus cavernosum

choices.label: D
choices.text: It directly stimulates nitric oxide synthase in the vascular endothelium

choices.label: E
choices.text: It increases release of nitric oxide from penile smooth muscle

explanation.summary: PDE-5 inhibitors block the enzyme that degrades cGMP, prolonging smooth muscle relaxation and blood flow.
explanation.whyCorrect: Under normal circumstances PDE-5 degrades cGMP, which would decrease smooth muscle relaxation and blood flow. By blocking PDE-5, these drugs reduce cGMP breakdown, leading to prolonged smooth muscle dilation in response to nitric oxide and increased blood flow in the corpus cavernosum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Guanylyl cyclase is activated by nitric oxide, not by PDE-5 inhibitors; the drugs do not increase cGMP production.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The drugs promote vasodilation and increased blood flow, not vasoconstriction, in the corpus cavernosum.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PDE-5 inhibitors do not stimulate nitric oxide synthase; they act downstream on cGMP metabolism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PDE-5 inhibitors do not increase nitric oxide release; they prolong the effect of cGMP already generated by the NO pathway.

questions.stem: During the normal male sexual response, nitric oxide is released and activates an enzyme that converts GTP to cGMP, leading to smooth muscle relaxation. Which enzyme is directly activated by nitric oxide?

explanation.summary: Nitric oxide activates guanylyl cyclase, which converts GTP to cGMP to relax smooth muscle.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick teaches that nitric oxide activates guanylyl cyclase, which converts GTP to cGMP; the net result is relaxation of smooth muscle and increased blood flow needed for an erection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adenylyl cyclase generates cAMP, not cGMP, and is not the target of nitric oxide here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CYP3A4 is a metabolic enzyme in the liver, not part of the cGMP-generating pathway.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nitric oxide synthase produces nitric oxide; it does not convert GTP to cGMP.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Phosphodiesterase type 5 degrades cGMP rather than producing it.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man asks his physician for an erectile dysfunction medication that will give him the largest possible window of time for sexual activity after a single dose. Which of the following PDE-5 inhibitors has the longest duration of action, up to 36 hours?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All four have an equal duration of action

explanation.summary: Tadalafil has the longest duration of action, up to 36 hours, giving the widest window for sexual activity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the four PDE-5 inhibitors, tadalafil has the longest time frame of efficacy, up to 36 hours, which gives the patient a much larger window for sexual activity relative to the others.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The durations differ substantially, ranging from about 4 hours for sildenafil to 36 hours for tadalafil.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Avanafil has a duration of action of about 6 hours.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sildenafil has a duration of action of about 4 hours, the shortest of the group.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vardenafil has a duration of action of about 7 hours.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man taking sublingual nitroglycerin for angina also took sildenafil earlier the same evening. He now presents with lightheadedness and a blood pressure of 78/44 mm Hg. Which of the following best explains this dangerous interaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct vasoconstriction of coronary arteries causing ischemia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excessive increase in cardiac contractility raising myocardial oxygen demand

choices.label: C
choices.text: Induction of CYP3A4 that accelerates nitrate metabolism

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reflex tachycardia that raises cardiac output and blood pressure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Synergistic increases in cGMP producing profound vasodilation

explanation.summary: Nitrates and PDE-5 inhibitors act synergistically to raise cGMP, causing profound vasodilation and hypotension.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nitrates are converted to nitric oxide and raise cGMP, while PDE-5 inhibitors prevent cGMP breakdown. Together they act synergistically to cause significant vasodilation and ultimately dramatic reductions in blood pressure, so the two classes should never be taken at the same time.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both drugs cause vasodilation, not coronary vasoconstriction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The interaction lowers blood pressure through vasodilation; it does not primarily increase cardiac contractility.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The dangerous effect is a pharmacodynamic synergy on cGMP and blood pressure, not accelerated nitrate metabolism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The hallmark of this interaction is hypotension from vasodilation, not a compensatory rise in blood pressure.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man taking a PDE-5 inhibitor for erectile dysfunction reports new indigestion and a burning sensation of acid coming back up into his throat. Which of the following best explains this adverse effect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delayed gastric emptying causing food to remain in the stomach

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct erosion of the gastric mucosa by the drug

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased secretion of gastric acid by parietal cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Overproduction of cGMP within the gastric wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter

explanation.summary: Dyspepsia from PDE-5 inhibitors results from relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter and acid reflux.
explanation.whyCorrect: PDE-5 inhibitors relax smooth muscle, including the lower esophageal sphincter. This relaxation allows gastric acid to reflux into the esophagus, producing dyspepsia (indigestion or upset stomach).

whyWrongByChoice.A: The brick attributes dyspepsia to lower esophageal sphincter relaxation, not delayed gastric emptying.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The mechanism is smooth muscle relaxation and reflux, not direct erosion of the gastric mucosa.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dyspepsia here is due to reflux from sphincter relaxation, not increased acid secretion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The symptom results from smooth muscle relaxation permitting reflux, not from local overproduction of cGMP in the stomach.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old man who took a PDE-5 inhibitor several hours ago now has a painful erection that has persisted for more than 4 hours. This finding represents which of the following adverse effects, for which he should seek prompt medical attention?

explanation.summary: An erection lasting more than 4 hours is priapism, a medical emergency requiring prompt attention.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients taking PDE-5 inhibitors should be aware of priapism, an erection lasting over 4 hours. If this occurs the patient should seek medical attention, as it often requires a procedure to drain blood from the corpus cavernosum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dyspepsia is indigestion from lower esophageal sphincter relaxation, not a prolonged erection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Dysuria (painful urination) is not the adverse effect described and is not a recognized effect of these drugs here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Flushing is a common mild vasodilatory effect, not a prolonged painful erection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hypotension is low blood pressure from vasodilation, unrelated to the duration of an erection.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man with chronic stable angina and a prior myocardial infarction takes isosorbide mononitrate 60 mg daily. At a follow-up visit he reports erectile dysfunction over the past year and asks about medication. Which of the following is the most appropriate recommendation?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Start any PDE-5 inhibitor as long as it is separated from the nitrate by 2 hours

choices.label: C
choices.text: Start sildenafil at a low dose taken at the same time as his nitrate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Start tadalafil because its long half-life makes it safest with nitrates

choices.label: E
choices.text: Start vardenafil since it is not affected by fatty meals and avoids interactions

explanation.summary: PDE-5 inhibitors are contraindicated in patients receiving any form of nitrate due to profound hypotension.
explanation.whyCorrect: PDE-5 inhibitors and nitrates act synergistically to cause dramatic reductions in blood pressure. Because this patient takes isosorbide mononitrate, PDE-5 inhibitors should not be prescribed; they must not be used concurrently with any form of nitrate.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A 2-hour separation is insufficient; no PDE-5 inhibitor should be used within 24 hours of nitrate therapy, and longer for tadalafil.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Taking sildenafil at the same time as a nitrate is exactly the dangerous combination that must be avoided.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tadalafil is not safer with nitrates; its prolonged half-life actually means an even longer interval is needed before a nitrate can be given.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The food effect is irrelevant; vardenafil is still contraindicated with nitrates because of the hypotension risk.

questions.stem: A 59-year-old man who takes sildenafil is prescribed clarithromycin, a macrolide antibiotic that inhibits CYP3A4, for a respiratory infection. Which of the following is the most likely consequence of this combination?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Complete inactivation of sildenafil before it reaches the circulation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion of sildenafil into an active nitrate metabolite

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enhanced or prolonged sildenafil effect due to reduced metabolism

choices.label: D
choices.text: No interaction because sildenafil is eliminated only by the kidneys

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced sildenafil effect due to enzyme induction

explanation.summary: CYP3A4 inhibitors reduce metabolism of sildenafil, enhancing or prolonging its effect.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sildenafil, tadalafil, and vardenafil are metabolized via CYP3A4, and their effects may be enhanced or prolonged in patients who receive inhibitors of this enzyme. Macrolide antibiotics such as clarithromycin are common CYP3A4 inhibitors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Inhibiting CYP3A4 increases drug exposure rather than inactivating the drug before it reaches the circulation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: PDE-5 inhibitors are not converted into nitrate metabolites; the interaction is a reduction in metabolism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Although renal dose adjustment applies, sildenafil is metabolized by CYP3A4, so this metabolic interaction is clinically important.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A CYP3A4 inhibitor slows metabolism and increases drug levels; it does not induce the enzyme or reduce the effect.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man with chronic kidney disease needs treatment for erectile dysfunction. His physician notes that all PDE-5 inhibitors are eliminated renally and require dose adjustment, but one is of particular concern for toxicity from accumulation because of its prolonged half-life. Which drug is this?

choices.label: B
choices.text: None of them require renal dose adjustment

explanation.summary: Tadalafil's long half-life makes it the most concerning for accumulation and toxicity in renal impairment.
explanation.whyCorrect: All PDE-5 inhibitors are eliminated renally, so doses must be lowered when renal function is decreased. Tadalafil, because of its long half-life, is the most concerning for toxicity due to accumulation in patients with altered kidney function.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Avanafil has a duration of about 6 hours and a rapid onset; it is not the primary accumulation concern.
whyWrongByChoice.B: All of the PDE-5 inhibitors are eliminated renally and require dose reduction in renal impairment.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sildenafil has a much shorter duration of action (about 4 hours) and is less prone to accumulation than tadalafil.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vardenafil has a duration of about 7 hours and is not the drug singled out for accumulation risk.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old man who frequently eats high-fat meals wants a PDE-5 inhibitor whose absorption will not be reduced by fatty food. Which of the following best fits this requirement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All PDE-5 inhibitors are equally reduced by fatty meals

explanation.summary: Among the four PDE-5 inhibitors, only tadalafil's absorption is not affected by a fatty meal.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the comparison of PDE-5 inhibitors, the absorption of sildenafil, vardenafil, and avanafil is reduced by fatty meals, whereas tadalafil is not affected by fatty meals.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tadalafil is the exception whose absorption is not reduced by fatty meals, so they are not all equal.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Avanafil absorption is reduced by a fatty meal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sildenafil absorption is reduced by a fatty meal.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vardenafil absorption is reduced by a fatty meal.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man starting a PDE-5 inhibitor asks what side effects he is most likely to notice. Which of the following are the most common adverse effects of this drug class, all caused by vasodilation?

explanation.summary: The most common adverse effects of PDE-5 inhibitors are headache, flushing, and dizziness from vasodilation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Similar to the nitrate medications, the most common adverse effects associated with PDE-5 inhibitors are headache, flushing, and dizziness, all resulting from the vasodilation these drugs cause.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bradycardia, constipation, and dry mouth are not the vasodilatory effects described for PDE-5 inhibitors.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cough and bronchospasm are not the common adverse effects taught for this class.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PDE-5 inhibitors cause hypotension rather than hypertension because of vasodilation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Weight gain, edema, and hyperglycemia are not associated with PDE-5 inhibitors in this brick.

questions.stem: Before its use in erectile dysfunction was discovered, sildenafil was first studied and used as a mainstay of treatment for another condition, with erections noted as a side effect during those trials. For which condition was sildenafil originally studied?

explanation.summary: Sildenafil was first studied for pulmonary arterial hypertension, where its erectile side effect was noticed.
explanation.whyCorrect: PDE-5 inhibitors are a mainstay of treatment for pulmonary arterial hypertension. Sildenafil was first studied for this indication, and male patients were found to experience erections as a side effect, which led to its use in erectile dysfunction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Benign prostatic hyperplasia is not the original indication described for sildenafil in this brick.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chronic stable angina is treated with nitrates, not with the original sildenafil indication described here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Congestive heart failure is not the condition for which sildenafil was first studied.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sildenafil was studied for pulmonary arterial hypertension, not essential systemic hypertension.

questions.stem: A 49-year-old man with erectile dysfunction wants a PDE-5 inhibitor that begins working within about 30 minutes but whose effect wears off within the same day, because he is uneasy about a drug that lingers for a day or more. He rarely eats large meals. Which of the following best meets these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any of the four, since they share the same onset and duration

explanation.summary: Avanafil combines a 0.5-hour onset with a 6-hour duration of action.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the comparison table, avanafil has an onset of action of 0.5 hour and a duration of about 6 hours. It is the only agent that pairs the rapid half-hour onset with a duration that ends the same day.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The four PDE-5 inhibitors differ substantially in onset (0.5 to 1 hour) and duration (4 to 36 hours).
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sildenafil's onset of action is about 1 hour, not half an hour, although its 4-hour duration is short.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tadalafil also has a 0.5-hour onset, but its duration of action is up to 36 hours, which is exactly the prolonged effect this patient wants to avoid.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vardenafil's onset of action is about 1 hour, with a duration of about 7 hours.

questions.stem: A 56-year-old man is prescribed sildenafil for erectile dysfunction and asks how long before sexual activity he should take the tablet. Based on the drug's onset of action, which of the following is the most appropriate advice?

explanation.summary: Sildenafil has an onset of action of about 1 hour.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pharmacokinetic comparison lists sildenafil's onset of action as 1 hour, so the drug should be taken roughly an hour before anticipated sexual activity.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Four hours is sildenafil's duration of action, not its onset; by 4 hours the effect is ending.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Seven hours corresponds to vardenafil's duration of action, not to any drug's onset.
whyWrongByChoice.D: No PDE-5 inhibitor acts within 10 minutes; the fastest agents (tadalafil, avanafil) take about half an hour.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Twenty-four hours is the interval that must separate a PDE-5 inhibitor from nitrate therapy; it is not a dosing-to-activity interval.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man has been satisfied with sildenafil, which he takes about 1 hour before intercourse, except that its roughly 4-hour duration feels too short. He would like an alternative with a similar onset but a longer duration that still does not extend beyond a day. Which of the following is the most appropriate choice?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sildenafil taken with a fatty meal

explanation.summary: Vardenafil shares sildenafil's 1-hour onset but lasts about 7 hours.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vardenafil has an onset of action of 1 hour, the same as sildenafil, but its duration of action is about 7 hours rather than 4, and it does not extend into the next day.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Avanafil has a faster onset (0.5 hour) and a 6-hour duration, but the patient asked for an onset similar to sildenafil.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Two PDE-5 inhibitors should never be used at the same time because of the risk of profound hypotension.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A fatty meal reduces sildenafil absorption; it does not lengthen the duration of action.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tadalafil's onset is 0.5 hour and its duration is up to 36 hours, which extends beyond a day.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man asks for a PDE-5 inhibitor with the fastest possible onset. He explains that he usually takes the tablet after a large restaurant dinner that is high in fat. Which of the following is the most appropriate choice?

explanation.summary: Tadalafil is the only agent with a 0.5-hour onset whose absorption is not affected by fatty meals.
explanation.whyCorrect: Two drugs have a 0.5-hour onset of action, tadalafil and avanafil. Of these, only tadalafil's absorption is unaffected by a fatty meal; avanafil, like sildenafil and vardenafil, has reduced absorption with fatty meals.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Avanafil has a 0.5-hour onset, but its absorption is reduced by fatty meals, so a high-fat dinner would blunt its effect.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Sildenafil has a 1-hour onset and its absorption is reduced by fatty meals.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Two PDE-5 inhibitors must never be used at the same time because of the risk of profound hypotension.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vardenafil has a 1-hour onset and its absorption is reduced by fatty meals.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old man takes tadalafil for erectile dysfunction. Not realizing it is the same class of drug, he also takes a sildenafil tablet given to him by a friend before sexual activity. Which of the following adverse outcomes is he at greatest risk for?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Loss of efficacy from competition at PDE-5

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced tadalafil levels from enzyme induction

explanation.summary: Two PDE-5 inhibitors should never be used at the same time because of the risk of profound hypotension.
explanation.whyCorrect: PDE-5 inhibitors cause vasodilation and can lower blood pressure. Combining two agents of the class compounds this effect, so two PDE-5 inhibitors should never be used at the same time due to the risk of profound hypotension.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dyspepsia with these drugs results from lower esophageal sphincter relaxation, not acid secretion, and is not the concern with duplicate therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Two drugs acting on the same enzyme do not cancel each other; the combined effect is excessive, not diminished.
whyWrongByChoice.C: PDE-5 inhibitors do not increase cGMP synthesis; they reduce its breakdown. The specific hazard of combining two agents is hypotension.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neither drug induces the other's metabolism; the interaction is pharmacodynamic.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with hypertension and benign prostatic hyperplasia takes an alpha-1 blocker. He is now prescribed sildenafil for erectile dysfunction. Which of the following is the most important precaution with this combination?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Avoid the combination because alpha-1 blockers inhibit CYP3A4

choices.label: B
choices.text: Exercise caution because profound hypotension can occur

choices.label: C
choices.text: No precaution is needed because alpha-1 blockers do not interact

choices.label: D
choices.text: Separate the two drugs by 24 hours as is done with nitrates

choices.label: E
choices.text: Switch to tadalafil because it does not lower blood pressure

explanation.summary: PDE-5 inhibitors combined with other blood pressure lowering agents, including alpha-1 blockers, can cause profound hypotension.
explanation.whyCorrect: Caution must be exercised when giving PDE-5 inhibitors with other blood pressure lowering agents, including alpha-1 blockers, because profound hypotension could occur. The drug's own hypotensive effect is generally mild, but it can become severe when combined with other medications.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The interaction with alpha-1 blockers is additive blood pressure lowering, not CYP3A4 inhibition.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Alpha-1 blockers are specifically named as blood pressure lowering agents that warrant caution with PDE-5 inhibitors.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The 24-hour separation rule applies to nitrates; with alpha-1 blockers the guidance is caution, not a fixed interval.
whyWrongByChoice.E: All PDE-5 inhibitors cause vasodilation and can lower blood pressure; tadalafil is not exempt.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man takes sildenafil and then drinks several alcoholic beverages at a party. Later in the evening he becomes lightheaded and faints. Which of the following best explains this event?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Alcohol causes vasodilation that adds to the drug's hypotensive effect

choices.label: B
choices.text: Alcohol inhibits hepatic CYP3A4 and raises sildenafil plasma levels

choices.label: C
choices.text: Alcohol reduces sildenafil absorption from the gut like a fatty meal

choices.label: D
choices.text: Alcohol relaxes the lower esophageal sphincter, causing reflux and dyspepsia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Alcohol triggers priapism with resulting blood loss and hypotension

explanation.summary: Alcohol also causes vasodilation, and combined with a PDE-5 inhibitor it can produce hypotension and syncope.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients taking a PDE-5 inhibitor should be very cautious of alcohol intake. Alcohol can also cause vasodilation, and when combined with a PDE-5 inhibitor, hypotension can occur, putting the patient at risk for fainting or syncope.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The listed CYP3A4 inhibitors are macrolides, azole antifungals, antiretrovirals, and grapefruit juice; the alcohol interaction is additive vasodilation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reduced absorption would lessen the drug effect, not produce hypotension and syncope.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lower esophageal sphincter relaxation explains dyspepsia, not fainting.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Priapism is a prolonged erection, not a cause of syncope, and is not linked to alcohol here.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man who takes tadalafil begins drinking a large glass of grapefruit juice every morning. He notices that his headache and flushing after each dose have become more intense and last longer than before. Which of the following best explains this change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Grapefruit juice acts as an alpha-1 blocking agent

choices.label: B
choices.text: Grapefruit juice enhances tadalafil absorption from the gut

choices.label: C
choices.text: Grapefruit juice increases renal elimination of the drug

choices.label: D
choices.text: Grapefruit juice inhibits CYP3A4 and reduces tadalafil metabolism

choices.label: E
choices.text: Grapefruit juice is a dietary source of nitrates

explanation.summary: Grapefruit juice is a CYP3A4 inhibitor that enhances or prolongs the effects of tadalafil.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sildenafil, tadalafil, and vardenafil are metabolized via CYP3A4, and their effects may be enhanced or prolonged in patients receiving inhibitors of this enzyme. Grapefruit juice is listed among the common CYP3A4 inhibitors along with macrolides, azole antifungals, and antiretrovirals.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Grapefruit juice has no alpha-1 blocking activity; it interacts through CYP3A4 inhibition.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The interaction involves reduced metabolism, not increased absorption.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Increased elimination would shorten and weaken the effect, the opposite of what occurred.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Grapefruit juice is not a nitrate; the interaction is metabolic, not the synergistic cGMP interaction seen with nitrates.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old man taking sildenafil asks which foods or medicines might intensify or prolong the drug's effect. Which of the following would NOT be expected to enhance or prolong the effect of sildenafil?

explanation.summary: A fatty meal reduces sildenafil absorption, whereas CYP3A4 inhibitors enhance or prolong its effect.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sildenafil's absorption is reduced by fatty meals, which would diminish rather than enhance its effect. In contrast, macrolide antibiotics, azole antifungals, antiretroviral agents, and grapefruit juice are all CYP3A4 inhibitors that can enhance or prolong the effects of sildenafil.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Macrolide antibiotics are common CYP3A4 inhibitors that enhance or prolong sildenafil's effect.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Antiretroviral agents are listed as CYP3A4 inhibitors that enhance or prolong the drug's effect.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Azole antifungals inhibit CYP3A4 and can enhance or prolong the drug's effect.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Grapefruit juice inhibits CYP3A4 and can enhance or prolong sildenafil's effect.

questions.stem: A 59-year-old man presents to the emergency department with chest pain, and the ECG shows ischemic changes. On questioning he reports having taken sildenafil about 6 hours earlier. Which of the following is the most appropriate approach to nitrate therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Give isosorbide mononitrate rather than nitroglycerin to avoid the interaction

choices.label: B
choices.text: Give nitroglycerin at a reduced dose to offset the interaction

choices.label: C
choices.text: Give nitroglycerin now because sildenafil's 4-hour duration of action has passed

choices.label: D
choices.text: Withhold nitrates because a PDE-5 inhibitor was used within the past 24 hours

choices.label: E
choices.text: Withhold nitrates until 12 hours after the sildenafil dose, then give them

explanation.summary: No nitrate should be started within 24 hours of a PDE-5 inhibitor dose.
explanation.whyCorrect: No PDE-5 inhibitor should be used in the 24 hours prior to initiating nitrate therapy, because the two act synergistically to produce profound increases in cGMP, significant vasodilation, and dramatic reductions in blood pressure. A dose 6 hours ago falls well within that window.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The contraindication applies to any form of nitrate, not only nitroglycerin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Dose reduction does not make the combination safe; nitrates and PDE-5 inhibitors must not be used concurrently.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The duration of erectile efficacy is not the safety interval; the 24-hour rule governs nitrate use after any PDE-5 inhibitor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The required interval is 24 hours, not 12.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man took tadalafil 30 hours ago and now presents with chest pain consistent with angina. The team considers giving nitroglycerin. Which of the following is the most accurate statement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Give nitrates at a reduced dose; the interaction with tadalafil is only mild dyspepsia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Give nitrates; tadalafil is eliminated renally, so it does not interact with nitrates

choices.label: C
choices.text: Give nitrates; tadalafil's 36-hour window refers only to erectile efficacy, not blood pressure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Give nitrates; the standard 24-hour interval after any PDE-5 inhibitor has been exceeded

choices.label: E
choices.text: Withhold nitrates; tadalafil's prolonged half-life may require an interval longer than 24 hours

explanation.summary: Because of tadalafil's prolonged half-life, more than 24 hours may be needed before a nitrate can be given.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although the general rule is that no PDE-5 inhibitor should be used within 24 hours before initiating nitrate therapy, a period longer than 24 hours may be needed following administration of tadalafil due to its prolonged half-life. This is why tadalafil presents a challenge in patients with cardiovascular comorbidities.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The interaction is dramatic reduction in blood pressure, not dyspepsia, and reduced dosing does not make it safe.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Renal elimination does not eliminate the interaction; all PDE-5 inhibitors act synergistically with nitrates on cGMP.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tadalafil's long duration reflects its extended half-life, which also prolongs the hypotensive interaction risk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The 24-hour interval is the general rule, but tadalafil specifically requires a longer period because of its prolonged t1/2.

questions.stem: Nitrates are converted to nitric oxide, which increases the amount of circulating cGMP in smooth muscle. cGMP then modulates the activity of phosphodiesterases to increase vasodilation. Which phosphodiesterase types are primarily involved in this process in smooth muscle?

explanation.summary: cGMP primarily modulates phosphodiesterases 2, 3, and 5 in smooth muscle.
explanation.whyCorrect: As nitrates are converted to nitric oxide, circulating cGMP increases. cGMP modulates the activity of phosphodiesterases, primarily types 2, 3, and 5, in smooth muscles, which increases vasodilation and blood flow. PDE-5 inhibitors act on the same pathway but at a different point, blocking PDE-5 specifically.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Types 1, 4, and 6 are not the isoforms described as primarily modulated by cGMP in smooth muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Type 3 is involved, but type 4 is not, and types 2 and 5 are omitted.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Types 4 and 7 are not the isoforms named in this pathway.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PDE-5 is the target of the inhibitor drugs, but cGMP itself primarily modulates types 2, 3, and 5.

questions.stem: A pharmacology student asks why an orally administered PDE-5 inhibitor preferentially increases blood flow in the corpus cavernosum rather than dilating all vascular beds to the same degree. Which of the following best explains this relative selectivity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Guanylyl cyclase is present only in penile endothelium

choices.label: B
choices.text: The drug is activated by an enzyme expressed only in the penis

choices.label: C
choices.text: The drug is actively transported into the corpus cavernosum

choices.label: D
choices.text: The drug stimulates nitric oxide release only in penile tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: There is a large concentration of PDE-5 within penile smooth muscle

explanation.summary: PDE-5 is highly concentrated in the smooth muscle of the penis, so inhibiting it preferentially increases penile blood flow.
explanation.whyCorrect: There is a large concentration of PDE-5 within the smooth muscle of the penis. Consequently, PDE-5 inhibitors increase blood flow in the corpus cavernosum, decreasing vascular resistance and increasing erectile function, even though some systemic vasodilation (headache, flushing, mild hypotension) still occurs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nitric oxide and guanylyl cyclase operate in vascular smooth muscle broadly, which is why systemic vasodilatory effects occur.
whyWrongByChoice.B: PDE-5 inhibitors are not prodrugs requiring local activation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Selectivity is due to the distribution of the target enzyme, not active drug transport.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PDE-5 inhibitors do not stimulate nitric oxide release; they prolong the response to nitric oxide by reducing cGMP breakdown.

questions.stem: During a normal erection, nitric oxide-mediated relaxation of arterial smooth muscle allows blood to flow into two spongy tubular vessels that run the length of the penis; when these fill with blood the penis becomes hard and erect. Which of the following structures is being described?

explanation.summary: The corpora cavernosa are the paired spongy vessels that fill with blood to produce an erection.
explanation.whyCorrect: The corpora cavernosa (plural) are the two spongy tubular vessels that run down the length of the penis. When these vessels are filled with blood, the penis is hard and erect. Nitric oxide activates guanylate cyclase, raising cGMP, relaxing arterial smooth muscle so blood flows into these vessels.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The prostate is a gland, not a blood-filled erectile vessel.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The seminal vesicles are secretory glands, not erectile tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The urethra conducts urine and semen; it is not the spongy vessel that fills to produce rigidity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The vas deferens carries sperm; it does not fill with blood.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a painful erection that has persisted for 6 hours after he took vardenafil. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Administer a dose of a different PDE-5 inhibitor

choices.label: B
choices.text: Advise a fatty meal to reduce further drug absorption

choices.label: C
choices.text: Give sublingual nitroglycerin to reverse the effect

choices.label: D
choices.text: Perform a procedure to drain blood from the corpus cavernosum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reassure him that it will resolve once the 7-hour duration passes

explanation.summary: Priapism often requires a procedure to drain blood from the corpus cavernosum.
explanation.whyCorrect: An erection lasting over four hours is priapism. The patient should seek medical attention, as it often requires a procedure to drain blood from the corpus cavernosum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Two PDE-5 inhibitors should never be used together and adding one would worsen, not treat, the problem.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Absorption has already occurred; a fatty meal has no role in treating priapism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nitrates are contraindicated within 24 hours of a PDE-5 inhibitor because of profound hypotension, and would not drain the trapped blood.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Priapism is a medical problem requiring intervention; waiting out the drug's duration is not the recommended approach.

questions.stem: A 57-year-old man taking no other medications is started on sildenafil. At a follow-up visit his blood pressure is 118/74 mm Hg, compared with 126/80 mm Hg before starting the drug, and he has no symptoms. Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A CYP3A4-mediated accumulation of the drug that requires discontinuation

choices.label: B
choices.text: An early sign of the profound hypotension seen when two PDE-5 inhibitors are combined

choices.label: C
choices.text: An expected mild blood pressure reduction that is typically not noticeable; no change needed

choices.label: D
choices.text: An indication to switch to tadalafil because of its shorter duration of action

choices.label: E
choices.text: Evidence that his renal function has declined and the dose must be lowered

explanation.summary: Hypotension from a PDE-5 inhibitor alone is generally mild and not noticeable.
explanation.whyCorrect: PDE-5 inhibitors can cause hypotension, but on their own this is generally mild and not noticeable. It becomes severe only when combined with other medications such as nitrates, other blood pressure lowering agents, or alcohol.

whyWrongByChoice.A: He takes no CYP3A4 inhibitors, and a small asymptomatic reduction does not indicate accumulation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: He takes only one PDE-5 inhibitor; a small asymptomatic decrease is the expected mild effect, not profound hypotension.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tadalafil has the longest duration (36 hours), not a shorter one, and there is no reason to switch.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nothing suggests renal decline; the mild drop is a known effect of the drug's vasodilation.

questions.stem: Four PDE-5 inhibitors are available to treat erectile dysfunction in the United States. Which two are by far the most commonly used?

explanation.summary: Sildenafil and tadalafil are by far the most commonly used PDE-5 inhibitors.
explanation.whyCorrect: The four PDE-5 inhibitors available in the United States are sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil, and avanafil. Sildenafil and tadalafil are by far the most commonly used.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Vardenafil is not among the two most commonly used; tadalafil is.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Avanafil is not among the two most commonly used; sildenafil is.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Vardenafil and avanafil are the two less commonly used agents.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vardenafil is not among the two most commonly used; sildenafil is.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man takes sildenafil about 1 hour before intercourse immediately after a large dinner of steak and fried foods and reports almost no effect. On previous occasions when he took the drug on an empty stomach it worked well. Which of the following best explains the difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delayed onset because sildenafil normally requires 4 hours

choices.label: B
choices.text: Development of tolerance to the drug

choices.label: C
choices.text: Food-induced increase in PDE-5 activity in the penis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased CYP3A4 metabolism induced by dietary fat

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced absorption of sildenafil because of the fatty meal

explanation.summary: Sildenafil's absorption is reduced by fatty meals.
explanation.whyCorrect: The absorption of sildenafil, vardenafil, and avanafil is affected by fatty meals; only tadalafil is unaffected. Taking sildenafil right after a high-fat meal reduces its absorption and therefore its effect.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sildenafil's onset of action is about 1 hour; 4 hours is its duration of action.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The drug worked well on prior occasions and the only change was the meal, pointing to absorption rather than tolerance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Food does not alter PDE-5 activity in penile smooth muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Dietary fat does not induce CYP3A4; the food effect is on absorption.

questions.stem: Nitrates and PDE-5 inhibitors both enhance cGMP-mediated smooth muscle relaxation but act at different points in the same pathway. Which of the following correctly contrasts their sites of action?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both nitrates and PDE-5 inhibitors increase cGMP formation by activating guanylyl cyclase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both nitrates and PDE-5 inhibitors prevent cGMP breakdown, at PDE-3 and PDE-5 respectively

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nitrates block breakdown of cGMP by PDE-5; PDE-5 inhibitors are converted to nitric oxide

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nitrates inhibit guanylyl cyclase; PDE-5 inhibitors activate guanylyl cyclase directly

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nitrates supply nitric oxide that increases cGMP formation; PDE-5 inhibitors prevent cGMP breakdown

explanation.summary: Nitrates raise cGMP production via nitric oxide, while PDE-5 inhibitors reduce cGMP degradation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nitrates are converted to nitric oxide, which activates guanylyl cyclase and increases circulating cGMP. PDE-5 inhibitors work on the same pathway but a different area: they block PDE-5, the enzyme that degrades cGMP. Because one increases production and the other blocks breakdown, the combination causes profound increases in cGMP.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Only nitrates (through nitric oxide) increase cGMP formation; PDE-5 inhibitors do not activate guanylyl cyclase.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nitrates do not inhibit a phosphodiesterase; they increase cGMP production upstream.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This reverses the roles; it is nitrates that become nitric oxide and PDE-5 inhibitors that block cGMP breakdown.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nitrates activate, not inhibit, guanylyl cyclase via nitric oxide, and PDE-5 inhibitors act downstream on cGMP degradation.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man with newly diagnosed chronic stable angina is being started on isosorbide mononitrate. He currently takes no medication for erectile dysfunction. Which of the following counseling points is most important to include when prescribing the nitrate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A PDE-5 inhibitor and the nitrate must be separated by at least 4 hours

choices.label: B
choices.text: A PDE-5 inhibitor is safe provided the nitrate is taken first each day

choices.label: C
choices.text: If he develops erectile dysfunction, a PDE-5 inhibitor may be used at half the usual dose

choices.label: D
choices.text: If he develops erectile dysfunction, avanafil is preferred because of its short duration

choices.label: E
choices.text: PDE-5 inhibitors must not be used concurrently with the nitrate at any time

explanation.summary: When prescribing nitrates, patients must be warned that PDE-5 inhibitors and nitrates cannot be used concurrently.
explanation.whyCorrect: PDE-5 inhibitors should not be prescribed to patients receiving any form of nitrate. In prescribing nitrates, the patient should be warned that PDE-5 inhibitors and nitrates must not be used concurrently and that no PDE-5 inhibitor should be used in the 24 hours prior to initiating nitrate therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The required separation before initiating nitrates is 24 hours (longer for tadalafil), and concurrent use is contraindicated outright.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Order of administration does not matter; the two classes act synergistically on cGMP whenever both are present.
whyWrongByChoice.C: No dose of a PDE-5 inhibitor is safe with concurrent nitrates; the combination causes dramatic reductions in blood pressure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The contraindication applies to all four PDE-5 inhibitors regardless of duration of action.

questions.stem: A pharmacist reviews the medication and diet history of a 64-year-old man who has just been prescribed sildenafil. Which of the following co-administered agents represents the MOST concerning interaction?

explanation.summary: The most concerning PDE-5 inhibitor interaction is with nitrates.
explanation.whyCorrect: PDE-5 inhibitors have several important interactions, but the most concerning interaction is between nitrates and PDE-5 inhibitors, which act synergistically to cause profound increases in cGMP, significant vasodilation, and dramatic reductions in blood pressure. Nitrates are an absolute contraindication rather than a caution.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Macrolides inhibit CYP3A4 and may enhance the drug's effect, a lesser concern than nitrates.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Alpha-1 blockers warrant caution for hypotension, but nitrates are the most concerning interaction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Grapefruit juice is a CYP3A4 inhibitor that may prolong the effect, but it is not the most dangerous interaction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Alcohol adds vasodilation and warrants caution, but nitrates are the most concerning interaction.

questions.stem: Most adverse effects of PDE-5 inhibitors result from vasodilation. Which of the following adverse effects instead results from relaxation of a non-vascular smooth muscle?

explanation.summary: Dyspepsia arises from relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter, not from vasodilation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Headache, flushing, dizziness, and hypotension are all due to the vasodilation these drugs cause. Dyspepsia, in contrast, is due to relaxation of the smooth muscles of the lower esophageal sphincter, which allows gastric acid to reflux into the esophagus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dizziness results from vasodilation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Flushing results from vasodilation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Headache is one of the most common adverse effects and results from vasodilation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hypotension results from vasodilation of the systemic vasculature.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man reports a 1-year history of difficulty achieving and maintaining erections sufficient for intercourse. Evaluation reveals no clear correctable cause. Which of the following drug classes is the most common treatment for this condition?

explanation.summary: PDE-5 inhibitors are the most common treatment for erectile dysfunction without a clear correctable cause.
explanation.whyCorrect: Erectile dysfunction is the inability to achieve or maintain an erection for sexual intercourse. The most common treatment for ED without a clear correctable cause is the phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE-5) inhibitors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alpha-1 blockers are blood pressure lowering agents that require caution with PDE-5 inhibitors; they do not treat ED.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CYP3A4 inhibitors are drugs that interact with PDE-5 inhibitors, not a treatment for ED.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibiting guanylyl cyclase would reduce cGMP and impair, not improve, erection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nitrates treat angina and are contraindicated with PDE-5 inhibitors; they are not a treatment for ED.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman is diagnosed with pulmonary arterial hypertension. Her physician prescribes a drug class whose original clinical trials in this condition revealed an unexpected effect on male sexual function. Which of the following classes is a mainstay of treatment for her condition?

explanation.summary: PDE-5 inhibitors are a mainstay of treatment for pulmonary arterial hypertension as well as erectile dysfunction.
explanation.whyCorrect: PDE-5 inhibitors are used for erectile dysfunction, but they are also a mainstay of treatment for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Sildenafil was first studied only for PAH, and researchers found that male patients experienced erections as a side effect, leading to its second indication.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alpha-1 blockers are described only as blood pressure lowering agents that interact with PDE-5 inhibitors, not as PAH therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Azole antifungals are CYP3A4 inhibitors, not a treatment for PAH.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Macrolide antibiotics are CYP3A4 inhibitors that interact with PDE-5 inhibitors; they do not treat PAH.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nitrates are angina drugs that must not be combined with PDE-5 inhibitors; they are not the PAH mainstay described.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with essential hypertension is started on amlodipine. The drug lowers his blood pressure by acting on a specific membrane protein in vascular smooth muscle. Which of the following is the primary molecular target of this class of drugs?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ligand-gated potassium channel in the membrane

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sodium-potassium ATPase pump of the membrane

explanation.summary: Calcium channel blockers inhibit plasma-membrane voltage-gated L-type calcium channels.
explanation.whyCorrect: CCBs block or inhibit voltage-gated L-type calcium channels in the plasma membrane. Blocking the channel inhibits the influx of Ca2+ into the cell, reducing the intracellular calcium available for smooth muscle contraction and cardiac activity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ACE is the target of ACE inhibitors, which act on the renin-angiotensin system rather than calcium channels.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Beta-1 receptors are the target of beta-blockers, not CCBs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CCBs act on voltage-gated calcium channels, not on ligand-gated potassium channels.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The Na/K ATPase is inhibited by cardiac glycosides such as digoxin, not by CCBs.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation and a rapid ventricular response needs an agent that slows conduction through the AV node for rate control. Her physician selects a non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker. Which of the following drugs did the physician most likely choose?

explanation.summary: Verapamil and diltiazem are the non-dihydropyridine CCBs used for AV nodal rate control.
explanation.whyCorrect: CCBs are classified by chemical structure into dihydropyridines (DHPs) and non-dihydropyridines (non-DHPs). Verapamil is a non-DHP that potently suppresses SA and AV nodal activity, making it useful to control ventricular rate in atrial fibrillation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amlodipine ends in the '-dipine' suffix and is a DHP, which has minimal nodal effect.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Felodipine is a DHP with little AV nodal suppression.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nicardipine is a DHP and is not used primarily for AV nodal rate control.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nifedipine is a DHP and is a potent arterial vasodilator rather than a nodal agent.

questions.stem: In vascular smooth muscle, a rise in cytosolic calcium promotes contraction through a defined signaling cascade. By blocking calcium influx, CCBs prevent activation of the enzyme that phosphorylates myosin light chain. Which of the following best describes the step CCBs interrupt in this pathway?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Calcium binding to troponin C, exposing actin binding sites

choices.label: D
choices.text: Release of acetylcholine from parasympathetic terminals

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sodium influx through fast voltage-gated sodium channels

explanation.summary: In smooth muscle, Ca-calmodulin activates myosin light-chain kinase to drive contraction.
explanation.whyCorrect: In smooth muscle, increased cytosolic calcium binds calmodulin to form a Ca-calmodulin complex that activates myosin light-chain kinase. This kinase phosphorylates myosin light chain, facilitating actin-myosin interaction and sustained contraction. CCBs reduce calcium influx, decreasing this contractile process and relaxing vascular smooth muscle.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Troponin C is the calcium sensor in cardiac and skeletal muscle, not the calmodulin/MLCK pathway of smooth muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.C: cGMP breakdown by phosphodiesterase is the target of other vasodilators, not the step CCBs interrupt.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Acetylcholine release is unrelated to the intracellular calcium-calmodulin contractile mechanism blocked by CCBs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: CCBs act on calcium channels, not fast sodium channels.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man with newly diagnosed hypertension needs an agent whose predominant effect is potent arterial vasodilation with minimal effect on cardiac contractility or the SA node. Compared with the non-dihydropyridines, which class of CCB is the preferred antihypertensive because of this profile?

explanation.summary: Dihydropyridines are the most potent arterial vasodilators and are preferred antihypertensives.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the comparison of CCB effects, amlodipine (a DHP) has the highest arterial vasodilation potency while exerting minimal negative inotropic or chronotropic effect. Because DHPs are potent arterial vasodilators, they are preferred as antihypertensives compared with the non-DHPs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Beta-blockers act on adrenergic receptors, not calcium channels, and are outside this comparison.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Digoxin is not a calcium channel blocker and is not a preferred antihypertensive.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Diltiazem is a non-DHP with intermediate vasodilation and significant nodal effects.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Verapamil is a non-DHP whose strengths are nodal suppression and negative inotropy, not maximal vasodilation.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man with AV nodal reentrant tachycardia requires a calcium channel blocker with the greatest ability to suppress SA nodal firing (the most potent negative chronotropic agent). Which of the following drugs best fits this description?

explanation.summary: Verapamil has the strongest SA/AV nodal suppression among the CCBs.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the comparison of CCB effects, verapamil has the highest score for suppression of SA nodal (chronotropic) activity, making it the most potent negative chronotropic agent. Non-DHPs are used for their negative chronotropic and antiarrhythmic effects on slow-response nodal tissue.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amlodipine is a DHP with minimal nodal suppression.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Felodipine is a DHP with negligible effect on the SA node.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nicardipine is a DHP and does not suppress the SA node significantly.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nifedipine is a DHP and a potent vasodilator, not a nodal suppressant.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman is given an oral calcium channel blocker for hypertension. Shortly after dosing she develops palpitations, flushing, and a rapid heart rate. The rapid absorption and short half-life of the formulation she was given caused a sudden drop in blood pressure and a reflex sympathetic response. Which drug most likely caused these symptoms?

explanation.summary: Immediate-release nifedipine causes reflex tachycardia from its rapid, short-lived vasodilation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Immediate-release nifedipine is rapidly absorbed and has a short half-life (~1.8 h). This quick absorption causes a sudden drop in blood pressure that reflexively activates the sympathetic nervous system, producing tachycardia and flushing.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Amlodipine is absorbed slowly with a prolonged effect, so it produces little reflex tachycardia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Diltiazem is a non-DHP with nodal-slowing effects rather than reflex tachycardia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reflex tachycardia is characteristically less pronounced with other DHPs than with immediate-release nifedipine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Verapamil is a non-DHP that suppresses the SA node and would not cause reflex tachycardia.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man on amlodipine for hypertension develops bilateral ankle swelling. Laboratory studies show normal renal function, normal albumin, and no signs of heart failure. Which of the following best explains the mechanism of his peripheral edema?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increased venous capillary permeability from an allergic reaction

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lymphatic obstruction of the lower extremities

choices.label: C
choices.text: Precapillary arteriolar dilation raises capillary hydrostatic pressure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reduced plasma oncotic pressure from hypoalbuminemia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Renal sodium and water retention from decreased glomerular filtration

explanation.summary: CCB peripheral edema results from arteriolar dilation raising hydrostatic pressure, not fluid retention.
explanation.whyCorrect: The edema associated with CCBs is not due to fluid retention. CCBs dilate the arterial (precapillary) side, which increases hydrostatic pressure in the lower extremities, while the venous capillaries are not dilated. This imbalance raises capillary hydrostatic pressure and drives fluid into surrounding tissue.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Venous capillaries are not dilated by CCBs; the problem is arteriolar dilation, not allergic permeability.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lymphatic obstruction is not the mechanism of CCB-induced edema.
whyWrongByChoice.D: His albumin is normal, so reduced oncotic pressure does not explain the edema.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The edema is specifically not caused by renal fluid retention; renal function is normal here.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man treated for a supraventricular tachycardia reports worsening constipation since starting a calcium channel blocker. Which of the following agents is most likely responsible for this adverse effect?

explanation.summary: Constipation is a common adverse effect specifically associated with verapamil.
explanation.whyCorrect: Constipation is a common adverse drug reaction associated with verapamil, reflecting its relaxant effect on gastrointestinal smooth muscle. Verapamil is a non-DHP frequently used for supraventricular tachycardias.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amlodipine is a DHP more associated with peripheral edema than constipation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Felodipine is a DHP and is not the CCB classically linked to constipation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nicardipine is a DHP and is not the agent characteristically causing constipation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nifedipine is a DHP associated with reflex tachycardia and flushing, not typically constipation.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman on a calcium channel blocker is counseled to avoid grapefruit juice and is monitored when starting clarithromycin. These recommendations reflect a shared metabolic pathway of CCBs. Through which of the following mechanisms do these agents increase CCB levels?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Displacement of CCBs from plasma protein binding sites

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enhanced first-pass conversion of CCBs to active metabolites

choices.label: C
choices.text: Induction of CYP3A4, accelerating CCB clearance

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibition of CYP3A4, which normally metabolizes CCBs

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibition of renal tubular secretion of CCBs

explanation.summary: All CCBs are CYP3A4 substrates, so CYP3A4 inhibitors raise their levels.
explanation.whyCorrect: CCBs undergo extensive first-pass metabolism and are substrates of CYP3A4. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as macrolides (azithromycin, clarithromycin), certain antiretrovirals, and grapefruit juice reduce CCB metabolism, increasing their bioavailability and levels. These interactions are clinically relevant and should be monitored.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The interaction is metabolic (CYP3A4 inhibition), not protein-binding displacement.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Increased levels result from decreased metabolism, not enhanced conversion to active metabolites.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CYP3A4 induction would lower, not raise, CCB levels; grapefruit and macrolides inhibit the enzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.E: CCB levels rise through decreased hepatic metabolism, not reduced renal secretion.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old man with second-degree (Mobitz II) AV block and hypertension is being evaluated for antihypertensive therapy. Which of the following CCBs is contraindicated because it can further suppress AV nodal conduction?

explanation.summary: Non-DHPs are contraindicated in high-grade heart block because they suppress AV nodal conduction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Non-DHPs such as verapamil are contraindicated in patients with second- and third-degree heart block because they further suppress SA and AV nodal activity, which can worsen conduction disease. Diltiazem shares this contraindication.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amlodipine is a DHP with minimal nodal effect and does not carry this AV block contraindication.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Felodipine is a DHP without meaningful AV nodal suppression.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nicardipine is a DHP and does not worsen AV nodal conduction the way non-DHPs do.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nifedipine is a DHP that acts mainly as a vasodilator and does not significantly suppress the AV node.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man with stable angina is prescribed a CCB to reduce the frequency of his chest pain. The drug decreases cardiac contractility, lowering myocardial oxygen demand. Blockade of calcium influx in cardiac muscle produces this negative inotropic effect by preventing which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Breakdown of ATP by the sodium-potassium pump

choices.label: C
choices.text: Calcium-calmodulin activation of myosin light-chain kinase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Release of norepinephrine from sympathetic nerve terminals

explanation.summary: In cardiac muscle, CCBs reduce calcium available to bind troponin C, decreasing contractility.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cardiac muscle relies on calcium-induced calcium release, and calcium must bind troponin C to permit actin-myosin cross-bridging. By inhibiting calcium influx, CCBs reduce calcium binding to troponin C, producing more sustained relaxation and negative inotropy. Lower contractility decreases myocardial oxygen demand, which relieves angina.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The Na/K pump is unrelated to the negative inotropic action of CCBs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The calmodulin/myosin light-chain kinase pathway is the smooth muscle mechanism, not the cardiac contractile mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Funny (If) channels are sodium-carried pacemaker currents, not the calcium-troponin step targeted here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: CCBs do not act by blocking norepinephrine release; that is the mechanism of other drug classes.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man with hypertension is switched from immediate-release nifedipine to amlodipine to avoid the palpitations he experienced previously. Which pharmacokinetic property of amlodipine explains why it produces less reflex tachycardia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A very short half-life that clears the drug quickly

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lack of any first-pass hepatic metabolism

choices.label: C
choices.text: Renal elimination that avoids CYP3A4 metabolism

choices.label: D
choices.text: Selective suppression of the SA node like a non-DHP

choices.label: E
choices.text: Slow absorption and a prolonged effect

explanation.summary: Amlodipine's slow, prolonged absorption avoids the abrupt BP drop that triggers reflex tachycardia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Unlike immediate-release nifedipine, amlodipine is absorbed slowly and has a prolonged effect, reaching steady-state concentration gradually over roughly 7 to 10 days of daily dosing. This gradual profile lets the body adapt and is associated with less reflex tachycardia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A short half-life describes immediate-release nifedipine, which causes more reflex tachycardia, not less.
whyWrongByChoice.B: All CCBs undergo extensive first-pass metabolism, so amlodipine does not lack it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CCBs including amlodipine are CYP3A4 substrates; the benefit comes from slow absorption, not renal elimination.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Amlodipine is a DHP and does not suppress the SA node the way non-DHPs do.

questions.stem: Calcium acts as an important second messenger that controls processes ranging from gene transcription to apoptosis. Within the cell, the bulk of the calcium that is released to trigger these events is kept in a specific compartment and replenished by channels, pumps, and exchangers. Which of the following is the principal intracellular storage site for this calcium?

explanation.summary: Intracellular calcium is stored in the endoplasmic/sarcoplasmic reticulum.
explanation.whyCorrect: Calcium is an important second messenger that controls a myriad of cellular processes from gene transcription to apoptosis, and a rise in intracellular calcium initiates physiological processes such as muscle contraction and insulin release. Calcium is stored in the endoplasmic/sarcoplasmic reticulum (ER/SR), and these stores are replenished by calcium channels, pumps, and exchangers that line the plasma membrane or are expressed on the ER/SR.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The Golgi apparatus is not the calcium reservoir that channels, pumps, and exchangers replenish.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lysosomes are not the storage site for the calcium used as a second messenger.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The mitochondrial matrix is not the calcium store described; the ER/SR holds the releasable calcium pool.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The nuclear envelope is not identified as the calcium storage compartment.

questions.stem: A pharmacology student is studying the channels that calcium channel blockers inhibit. These channels selectively conduct calcium into the cell and are the focus of CCB pharmacology. Which of the following stimuli opens the calcium channels targeted by CCBs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A change in membrane potential during an action potential

choices.label: B
choices.text: A fall in the intracellular ATP concentration

choices.label: C
choices.text: Binding of an extracellular ligand such as acetylcholine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mechanical stretch of the plasma membrane bilayer

explanation.summary: CCBs target voltage-gated calcium channels, which open in response to action potential changes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The channels that CCBs act on are the calcium influx channels, mainly the voltage-gated calcium channels. Voltage-gated channels are activated by changes in the action potential and selectively conduct calcium into the cell (influx). Inhibiting these channels interferes with the cellular and physiological functions associated with increased intracellular calcium, which is the basis of CCB pharmacological activity.

whyWrongByChoice.B: ATP concentration governs ATP-sensitive channels, not the voltage-gated calcium channels targeted by CCBs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ligand binding opens ligand-gated channels; the channels CCBs block are voltage-gated.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mechanical stretch is not the activating stimulus for the voltage-gated L-type channels.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Kinase phosphorylation is not the gating stimulus described for these channels; they respond to membrane voltage.

questions.stem: L-type calcium channels are expressed in several organs beyond the heart and vascular smooth muscle. In one endocrine organ, calcium influx through these channels initiates the release of a hormone. Which of the following processes is initiated by L-type calcium influx in that organ?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aldosterone release from the adrenal cortex

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cortisol release from the adrenal cortex

explanation.summary: L-type calcium channels in the pancreas mediate calcium influx that initiates insulin secretion.
explanation.whyCorrect: L-type calcium channels are found in many organs, such as the heart, skeletal muscle, smooth muscle, and pancreas.
